title: The Space Shuttle Hit 17,000 mph and Air Heated to 3,000 Degrees

scenes.text: The space shuttle fell back to Earth at seventeen thousand miles an hour.
Squashing the air in front of it heated that air to about three thousand degrees Fahrenheit.
That's hot enough to melt steel.
So the underside was covered in silica tiles.
They conduct heat so badly that a tile could be held by its edges while red hot.
Hotter than lava outside. And the tile? You could hold it by the edges.

description:
The space shuttle re-entered the atmosphere at about 17,000 miles an hour.
Compressed air in front of it reached about 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit.
Silica tiles kept the metal skin safe.
Would you have flown it?
first_comment: Would you have flown the shuttle? What would scare you most?
